answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by requiring a costly, nontransferable deposit that is slashed when independent audits confirm coordinated duplicate identities. Auditors sample claims across the inlet and trace the same funding source, behavior, or reused credentials through a thread of linked accounts; a hollow profile with no history gets less weight until it earns trust over time. An attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it, so scaling a Sybil network becomes expensive rather than free.
